summary:
SPHERExLens is an open-source, automated discovery triage platform designed for NASA's SPHEREx near-infrared all-sky survey. It ingests Level-2 cutouts from NASA/IPAC IRSA, co-adds multi-detector exposures, applies ZOGY optimal image subtraction across observation epochs, and classifies candidates using a 102-band spectral classifier and a 22-feature gradient-boosted machine learning model.

Built specifically for the Planet X and SPHEREx track, the pipeline isolates moving infrared dipoles, such as slow-moving Planet X candidates or outer Solar System objects, and variable monopoles across 102 spectral channels. Detections are cross-matched against Gaia DR3, AllWISE, AAVSO VSX, and JPL Small-Body databases to separate known celestial bodies from uncatalogued targets, presenting prioritized candidates through an interactive web dashboard with human-in-the-loop vetting.

Manual inspection of millions of multi-epoch sky exposures is infeasible. SPHERExLens dramatically improves strict injection-recovery completeness from 0.2% to 69.3% while suppressing false alarms to 1.66 per field, enabling astronomers to reliably discover faint uncatalogued brown dwarfs, outer Solar System bodies, and dynamic cosmic anomalies.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

SPHERExLens operates as a six-stage automated pipeline integrated with an interactive web dashboard:

  • Data Ingest & Fetching: Automatically queries NASA/IPAC IRSA via SIA2 services to fetch Level-2 near-infrared FITS cutouts (including effective point spread functions and zodiacal-light models) alongside star catalogs. Detections are cross-matched against Gaia DR3, AllWISE, AAVSO VSX, and JPL Small-Body Database endpoints.
  • Flags Masking & Exposure Co-addition: Rejects corrupted pixels using FLAGS bitmasks (e.g. cosmic rays, hot/cold pixels, overflow, stray light) and reprojects exposures onto a common TAN spatial grid using inverse-variance weighting.
  • Image Subtraction (Detection): Executes Zackay–Ofek–Gal-Yam (ZOGY) optimal image subtraction between consecutive observation epochs to isolate moving dipoles (Planet X candidates or asteroids) and variable monopoles (brightening or fading stars).
  • Catalog Cross-Matching & Triage: Matches candidates within a 30-arcsecond search radius (5-arcsecond tight match radius) to categorize objects into KNOWN or CANDIDATE verdicts. It performs explicit asteroid trajectory lookups via JPL SSD and CADC SSOIS services.
  • Spectral Extraction & Machine Learning: Extracts flux across 102 spectral channels using a 3-index classifier. Candidates are evaluated by a 22-feature gradient-boosted real/bogus ML model and an aggregated 0–100 evidence score.
  • Injection-Recovery Validation: Plants synthetic moving and variable targets into real images to quantify completeness across signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and proper motion.
  • User Interface: Serves data through a FastAPI backend and a light-themed web dashboard featuring sky viewers, vetting cards, WiseView flipbooks, and cloud snapshot history.

2. Key System Benefits

  • Dramatic Improvement in Completeness: Boosts strict injection-recovery detection completeness from 0.2% to 69.3% overall (achieving 96.7% for brightening sources, 95.3% for fading sources, and 56.0% for moving objects).
  • Low False-Alarm Rate: Reduces candidate false alarms to 1.66 per field by setting a calibrated 6-sigma threshold via a null-test subtraction loop.
  • Real-Time Archive Streaming: Stream cutouts directly from IRSA into system RAM in under 46 seconds, eliminating local storage dependencies for on-demand sky field inspection.
  • Dual-Audience Usability: Offers Public Mode for simplified verdicts and Expert Mode for VOTable, CSV, IVOA cone search access, and provenance links.

3. Intended Astronomical Impact

  • Accelerating Discoveries: Enables astronomers to rapidly discover faint, uncatalogued outer Solar System bodies (including potential Planet X candidates), brown dwarfs (Y-dwarfs), variable stars, and rare cosmic transients across 102 infrared channels.
  • Crowdsourced Validation: Integrates public voting into the candidate vetting process, allowing community classifications to feed back into machine learning retraining pipelines.
  • Open Science Architecture: Serves as an open-source technical template for processing large-scale survey datasets via containerized or static deployments.

4. Tools, Coding Languages & Infrastructure Used

  • Languages: Python (42.2%), JavaScript (23.8%), TeX (23.9%), HTML (3.9%), CSS (4.8%), and HCL (1.2%).
  • Backend & Scientific Stack: Python 3.11/3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, PyVO, and Reproject.
  • Frontend Dashboard: Custom Vanilla JavaScript canvas renderer (app.js), HTML5, and CSS3 utilizing IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono typography.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: Docker, Docker Compose, Google Cloud Run, Netlify (signed proxy), Terraform, Fly.io, Railway, and Render.
  • Data Protocols & Formats: FITS (with WCS-WAVE tables), VOTable XML, Parquet, TAP, SIA2, and REST APIs (JPL SBDB, CADC SSOIS, VizieR, IRSA, MAST).

5. Creative & Innovative Aspects

  • Dual-Path Architecture: Seamlessly switches between zero-server-cost pre-rendered static snapshot hosting and live in-memory streaming from NASA archives.
  • Interactive Canvas Sky Viewer: Features pan/zoom canvas rendering with interactive layer toggling (Co-add, ZOGY Difference, Significance), coordinate crosshairs, and 14-day historical snapshot playback with purple dipole tracking trails.
  • Consolidated Multi-Catalog Evidence Scoring: Aggregates ML probabilities, catalog kinematics (Gaia/AllWISE), NEOWISE 14-year light curves, JPL asteroid positioning, and CADC NEOSSat optical checks into a single transparent 0–100 evidence score.

6. Key Engineering & Scientific Factors Considered

  • Bandwidth & Storage Constraints: Avoided downloading full 72 MB Level-2 FITS files by executing targeted 5 MB spatial cutouts streamed directly into memory.
  • Noise Calibration & Artifact Mitigation: Calibrated significance thresholding using null-test subtractions and implemented brightness-dependent star masks to stop saturated stars from blinding adjacent faint detections.
  • System Resilience & Fallbacks: Designed Multi-archive API fallback chains and explicit UI status indicators when JPL asteroid services are offline.
  • Standards & Accessibility: Verified WCAG 2.1 AA web accessibility compliance, provided full keyboard navigation support, and integrated standalone font stacks for offline usage.
